reason: The cited evidence confirms that the base alloy forms Cr/V-rich precipitates and shows negligible hardening (no dislocation loops) under irradiation, supporting the first two premises. However, the evidence does not mention Hf, its effects on lattice distortion, diffusion, grain boundary cohesion, or sintering, leaving the remaining premises unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: W38Ta36Cr15V11 forms Cr/V-rich precipitates under irradiation
W38Ta36Cr15V11 shows negligible irradiation hardening (no dislocation loops)
Hf addition can suppress Cr/V precipitation by increasing lattice distortion and altering diffusion
Hf addition improves grain boundary cohesion and sintering for bulk fabrication
The quinary alloy will retain negligible hardening at ~8 dpa
